justice: Continuous car parking on the right edge heavily prioritizes vehicle space, demonstrating poor equity in road resource distribution for pedestrians.
The complete absence of tactile paving on the walkable edges severely reduces fairness for visually impaired users.
The left-side pedestrian area is obstructed by parked scooters and signboards, hindering accessibility for wheelchair users and those with mobility issues.
safety: The lack of dedicated bike lanes forces moped riders and cyclists to share the main lane with motor vehicles, increasing collision risks.
Continuous on-street parking on the right side introduces a significant 'dooring' hazard for passing cyclists and scooters.
The absence of marked pedestrian crosswalks and traffic calming measures reduces crossing safety, particularly for elderly and adolescent pedestrians.
livability: Small storefronts visible on the left side provide basic community commercial services, supporting daily neighborhood needs.
The complete lack of public seating or gathering spaces limits social interaction opportunities, especially for older adults and teenagers.
The dense, mature street trees create a pleasant neighborhood environment that somewhat offsets the lack of pedestrian amenities.
sustainability: Large, mature street trees on both sides provide extensive green infrastructure, aiding in urban cooling and carbon sequestration.
The lack of dedicated public transit stops or active mobility lanes fails to actively support a shift toward low-carbon travel.
Extensive impermeable asphalt paving dominates the surface area, with no visible rain gardens or permeable materials for stormwater management.
aesthetics: The continuous, dense tree canopy forms a highly attractive green tunnel effect, providing strong visual appeal.
Cluttered parking of mopeds on the left and cars on the right detracts from the overall visual order and neatness of the streetscape.
Visible overhead utility wires crossing the street introduce visual clutter into the otherwise green skyline.
comfort: Abundant shade from the dense tree canopy provides excellent thermal comfort for all road users during hot weather.
The absence of benches or resting points creates physical discomfort for elderly pedestrians who may need frequent breaks.
The narrow and obstructed walking space on the left side may induce psychological discomfort and a feeling of spatial crowding for pedestrians.
walkability: The right side of the street completely lacks a sidewalk, with parked cars directly abutting the vegetation, eliminating pedestrian continuity.
The left-side pathway is highly fragmented by parked two-wheelers and shop spillover, making walking difficult for older adults and families with strollers.
No visible crossing facilities force pedestrians to jaywalk across a relatively wide road, severely reducing walkability.
bikeability: The absence of any protected or painted bike lanes strongly compromises the perceived and actual safety for cyclists of all ages.
The flat, paved asphalt surface provides a physically smooth ride with low rolling resistance for bicycles and mopeds.
The presence of roadside parking on the right and merging traffic potential creates high-stress conditions for vulnerable cyclists.
